title: ResurrectionFormal.lean (Package)

canonical_node.axiom: The Lean 4 type checker is the final arbiter of proof validity; a package that compiles with zero sorry and zero admit constitutes a verified proof system.
definitions: Assembly point: a file that imports all core modules and confirms they compile together.
Zero sorry: every theorem has an actual proof checked by Lean, no placeholders.
Zero admit: no unproved assumptions admitted.
Compiled clean: the build succeeds with no errors.
derivation: ResurrectionFormal.lean imports six modules: Core, StageMachine, Mapping, IsomorphismTest, BridgeMatrix, MaxwellTrinity.
If any imported theorem has an error or type mismatch, the build fails.
The DASHBOARD entry reports 287 theorems, 0 axioms, 0 sorry, 0 admit, 16 Lean files, compiled clean.
Therefore, the package is a formally verified proof suite.
canonical_node.action: Run `lake build` on the repository; if it succeeds with no errors, accept the package as formally verified.
boundary: Does not prove any theological claim by itself; it only confirms the internal consistency of the Lean proofs.
Does not assert that the proofs are sound in an external mathematical sense beyond Lean's type theory.
Does not claim that the imported modules are correct in their modeling of physics or theology.
test: Run `lake build` and check for zero errors.
Verify that the DASHBOARD entry matches the actual build output.
Check that no `sorry` or `admit` appears in any imported file.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a single entry point that, when compiled, demonstrates the entire proof suite is formally verified.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the verified status of all six modules by requiring them to compile together.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If removed, the package loses its unified verification claim; individual modules may still compile but the assembly proof is gone.

classification.recommended_atom_action: preserve as assembly point; verify build log independently

overstatement_risks: The document claims 'the proof' but the file itself is only an assembly point; the actual proofs are in imported modules.
The DASHBOARD entry is self-reported and not independently verified in this document.
The claim that 'the entire proof system compiles clean' depends on the correctness of the build environment and the imported files.
kill_conditions: If any imported module contains a `sorry` or `admit`.
If the build fails on a clean checkout.
If the DASHBOARD entry is inaccurate.

plain_summary: This document describes a Lean 4 package entry point that imports six modules and claims that the whole suite compiles with zero sorry/admit, thus constituting a formal proof. The node captures the assembly action and verification test, but the actual proof content resides in the imported modules.
